title: Inoculating and Harvesting Fungal Isolates on Cellophane Overlay
author: Jana M U'Ren
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qtedwje
materials: Sterilize the biosafety cabinet and preheat the bactoincinerator.

While the equipment is cooling, label the sides of 2 ml screwtop bead tubes with the following information: Name of isolate Tube number If it is for DNA or RNA Age of plate Type of media it was grown on Date Your initials

steps.title: Prepare Cellophane Squares
steps.instruction: Prepare and sterilize cellophane squares for the media plates.

substeps.instruction: Wipe down bench top and scissors with RNase away solution.
Cut cellophane into approximately 1 inch squares, ensuring they fit in a 60mm Petri dish.
Place ~75 pieces into a 250mL glass beaker.
Fill beaker with 100 mL nanopure water to fully cover the pieces.
Cover beaker with aluminum foil and autoclave indicator tape.
Autoclave for 30 minutes on liquid cycle at 121°C and allow to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Apply Cellophane to Media Plates
steps.instruction: Transfer sterile cellophane squares onto the center of media plates within a biosafety cabinet.

substeps.instruction: Pre-sterilize fine-point forceps by submerging in 95% EtOH and placing for 5 seconds in the hot bactoincinerator.
Retrieve media plates from refrigerator and remove from sleeves.
In the biosafety cabinet, remove the aluminum cover from the cellophane beaker and place it in the back of the cabinet.
Using sterilized, cooled forceps, remove one piece of cellophane per media plate (scooping a large portion to the glass wall first to facilitate removal).
Place the square of cellophane flat in the center of the plate, ensuring it does not hang over the edge.
Re-bag media and apply pink tape with initials and date to indicate cellophane has been added.
If cellophane remains in the beaker and sterility was maintained, replace the aluminum cover and store on a shelf; otherwise, wash the dish or re-autoclave if contaminated.

steps.title: Inoculate Fungal Isolates
steps.instruction: Transfer fungal mycelium onto the cellophane overlays.

substeps.instruction: Record the names of isolates to be inoculated in the lab notebook.
Retrieve media plates from refrigerator and label them with isolates (labeling in reverse order is recommended).
Pre-sterilize fine-point forceps by submerging in 95% EtOH and placing for 5 seconds in the hot bactoincinerator.
Remove the fungal isolate source plate from the stack, remove and discard the parafilm, and place it on the side of the hood.
Remove the top lid from the new agar plate containing the cellophane overlay, placing the lid so arms do not cross over plates.
Using a sterile scalpel, cut a small piece of mycelium/agar from the culture plate and transfer it to the center of the cellophane.
Replace the lid on the new cellophane plate and move it to the side of the hood.
Replace the lid on the source culture plate and stack it away from remaining samples.
Repeat the inoculation process for all isolates.
Parafilm Petri dishes with two layers of parafilm to ensure mycelium pieces do not move, then place on the proper culture tray.

steps.title: Harvest and Flash Freeze Mycelium
steps.instruction: Harvest fresh mycelial tissue and preserve it using liquid nitrogen.

substeps.instruction: Pre-sterilize fine-point forceps by submerging in 95% EtOH and placing for 5 seconds in the hot bactoincinerator.
Pour liquid nitrogen from the large dewar into a portable benchtop dewar.
Loosen caps of tubes for one isolate (e.g., all four vouchers for one isolate simultaneously).
Using a sterile scalpel, remove the plug used as the source inoculum and place it on the side of the plate to ensure only fresh mycelium (without agar) is collected.
Use the side of the forceps to lightly scrape the new mycelial tissue into a 'bundle' without tearing the cellophane.
Transfer the bundled tissue into a labeled tube using the scalpel or forceps and cap the tube.
Tap the tube on the benchtop to ensure tissue is at the bottom on the beads.
Flash freeze the tube by placing it in the liquid N in the portable dewar.
Repeat the harvesting and freezing process for all samples.
Remove tubes from the dewar using long forceps and place them in respective boxes in the -80°C freezer.

steps.title: Document Harvesting Information
steps.instruction: Update the spreadsheet with the following details: name of isolate, tube number, purpose (DNA or RNA), age of plate, type of media, date, and your name.
